source.snippet: Why three tools that 'work together' still break your business. Your MVP is live, users are signing up... [score 18, 6 comments, tag: architecture, backend, saas, startup]

problem_statement: Early-stage SaaS founders repeatedly discover that their initial stack of auth, payments, and database tools marketed as 'working together' creates integration breakage, vendor lock-in, and hidden operational costs that threaten the business as it scales past MVP.
target_segment: Solo founders and small technical teams (1-5 engineers) launching or scaling B2B/B2C SaaS products who self-manage their backend infrastructure.
notes: Score of 18 with 6 comments on dev.to indicates meaningful resonance among practitioners. Paying-buyer evidence: SaaS founders are already paying for Stripe, Auth0/Clerk, Supabase/PlanetScale etc. — the pain is coordination cost between paid tools. Opportunity: a backend integration audit service, a vetted starter-kit with pre-wired integrations, or a monitoring tool that detects cross-service breakage early. Recurring subscription model viable.
